Møller MH refers to Mads H. Møller, a Danish surgical researcher specializing in emergency surgery and peptic ulcers. He is not to be confused with other individuals who share the same initials. Møller is a central figure in the research ecosystem surrounding the Danish Emergency Surgery Database (Akut Kirurgi Databasen) and its predecessor, the Danish Clinical Register of Emergency Surgery [^src1]. He frequently appears as an author or co-author in the scientific publications that form the methodological and evidence-based foundation for the database's clinical quality indicators [^src1], [^src2].

A key aspect of Møller's work is his leadership of the [[pulp-trial|PULP trial]], a major research initiative that is heavily referenced in the database's reports to justify specific treatment goals and timeframes [^src1]. The annual reports of the Emergency Surgery Database build upon this foundational registry research to evaluate systematic challenges in emergency care, such as preoperative delays, rapid antibiotic administration, and regional variations in quality [^src1], [^src2]. 

Møller's chronological contributions to the field highlight his focus on preoperative delays and mortality. In 2008, he was involved in multiple presentations on preoperative delay and mortality in patients with perforated peptic ulcers at several major conferences, including UEGW, ISQua, DASAIM, the Danish Surgical Society's anniversary meeting, and Forskningen Dag [^src1]. This research culminated in 2009 with the publication of a clinical audit on preoperative delay in patients with perforated ulcers in the journal *Ugeskrift For Læger* [^src1]. His continued relevance to the field is evidenced by his citations in the reference lists of both the 2023 and 2024 annual reports for the database [^src1], [^src2].
